clue.text: Busy cooks entertaining party served up alcoholic dessert

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it read from the bottom to the top
a host entertaining guests has them inside the house, so one piece goes within another
to cook something is to work it over and change its form, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a ball is a grand dancing party

explanation.surface: Harried cooks at a party bring out a boozy pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Cooks looks like the people in the kitchen, but it is a verb telling you to rework the letters; party is a dance here, not a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabub is an old English pudding of whipped cream flavoured with sweet wine or sherry.

clue.text: Prevent vessels up-ending

indicators.note: upending something turns it upside down, so in a down entry the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: pots are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: An instruction not to let the boats capsize.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessels suggests ships, but here they are kitchen containers.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something happening is to prevent it; both are verbs of blocking an action.

clue.text: Pig stuffed with first of trimmings, cook meaty snack

indicators.note: something stuffed has a filling put inside it, so the outer piece wraps the others

parts.note: a hog is a pig

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: opening letter of the word
to do food is to cook it, as in 'do the vegetables'

explanation.surface: A recipe for a stuffed pig with all the trimmings.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook gives DO, as in 'do the vegetables', a sense solvers often miss; trimmings sounds like garnish but gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a sausage served in a long bread roll, a classic quick snack of meat.

clue.text: The Lord has plan for Semitic language

parts.note: He, capitalised, refers to God
to brew a scheme is to plan or plot it

explanation.surface: God has a scheme concerning an ancient language of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised pronoun HE is a common way of referring to God.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebrew belongs to the Semitic family of languages, along with Arabic and Aramaic.

clue.text: Pasta carbonara initially imported by Romania, surprisingly

indicators.note: goods imported by a country are brought inside it, so one piece goes within another
a surprising outcome is not the expected order of things, so the letters come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A news item: Romania has taken up the Italian pasta dish carbonara.
explanation.walkthrough: C is put inside ROMANIA and the whole lot rearranged; carbonara is a tempting distraction since it is itself a pasta sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a type of short, tubular Italian pasta.

clue.text: Coin on cross

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A coin balanced on a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross is a verb here, as in football: a winger centres or crosses the ball into the middle of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, to centre the ball is to cross it from the wing into the goal area.

clue.text: Books written after novel ready — long time ago

indicators.note: something written after another follows it, so this piece comes second
novel means new and different, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A novel was finished and books followed it, ages back.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a noun (a book) but acts as the rearrangement signal; Books is the standard OT, the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The year dot is an informal British idiom for a time very long ago, as if the first year of all.

clue.text: Cancel any new negotiations, until later, first of all

indicators.note: the first of all the words means the opening letter of every one of them

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A call to call off all fresh talks until some later date.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make it read as a diplomatic instruction, but only the initial letters of the five words count.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, which is to cancel it officially.

clue.text: Order change of cat diet

indicators.note: a change of something alters its makeup, so the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet's instruction to put the cat on a new diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Order looks like a noun, but as a verb it means to command.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to give an order with authority, as in dictating terms to a defeated side.

clue.text: Speak about exercise in work

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A suggestion to talk about workplace exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: Exercise is the school subject physical education, and about tells you to wrap the speaking verb around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that operates is functioning, so operate and work are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: French city has better device for photographer

parts.note: Lens is a town in northern France
to cap a remark is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A French city boasts a superior camera gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Better is a verb, as in capping someone's story; Lens is a mining town in the north of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens cap is the cover a photographer clips over the camera lens to protect it.

clue.text: Asleep in bed, or man trembling

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letters lie within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the words, ignoring spaces

explanation.surface: Someone lies in bed, either sleeping or a man shivering.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is found spanning the end of bed through the start of trembling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive as if sleeping, like a volcano or a seed waiting for spring.

clue.text: Note a swamp overwhelming new pool in Australia

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a bill is a banknote
taken as written
a bog is a swamp
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A swamp floods a new pool somewhere in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Note is money here, not music; N for new goes inside BOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is the Australian word for a stagnant pool or backwater cut off from a river.

clue.text: German physicist well meaning, originally

parts.note: well and oh are both exclamations of mild surprise

indicators.note: originally means at the origin or start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A German scientist who had good intentions from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Well-meaning reads as one phrase but splits into the exclamation and a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Ohm was the German physicist who stated the law of electrical resistance, and the unit is named after him.

clue.text: Entire space for the audience?

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a hole is an empty space or gap

explanation.surface: A question about whether the whole auditorium is for the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: Space suggests a theatre's seating, but it is a gap, and the answer sounds identical to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and entire both mean complete, with no part missing.

clue.text: Defensive strategy — of golfer in trap?

parts.note: straight sense: a siege attitude of seeing threats everywhere and digging in
playful sense: the state of mind of a golfer whose ball has landed in a sand trap

explanation.surface: A golfer stuck in the sand plots a cautious way out.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunker is both a military shelter and a golf course sand trap, so the phrase can be read as a golfer's frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunker mentality is a defensive, besieged attitude in which a group feels under constant attack.

clue.text: African country, Asian country not right

indicators.note: not having the right means lacking the letter used for right, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Niger is a country in West Africa
Iran is a country in western Asia

explanation.surface: A list of an African nation and an Asian one that is somehow wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: African country reads as one phrase, but African alone is the definition and country starts the wordplay; R for right leaves IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something Nigerian comes from Nigeria, a West African nation, so the adjective is a narrower form of African.

clue.text: Born in Eastbourne, Englishman

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the town and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: An Englishman whose birthplace is the seaside town of Eastbourne.
explanation.walkthrough: Eastbourne is a seaside resort on England's south coast; the answer spans its end and the start of Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name, as in 'Mrs Smith, née Jones'.

clue.text: Male blocks a more ghastly suitor

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something that blocks a passage sits in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: dire means dreadful, so direr is more ghastly
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man fends off a particularly hideous suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Blocks looks like it means stops, but it means sits inside: M lodges in A DIRER.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courts someone, and an admirer is a person romantically attracted to them, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Horse in grey lad cut off

indicators.note: cutting something off removes its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A boy dressed in grey gets his hair cut, or a horse is described.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate rearrangement word: the letters of IN GREY plus LA from the shortened lad are simply jumbled, so the clue relies on the solver spotting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a young horse in its second year, between one and two years old.

clue.text: Power in arachnid, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: judging by sound means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a mite is a tiny arachnid, related to spiders

explanation.surface: A question about how strong a spider sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Mites are arachnids, cousins of spiders and ticks, and their name sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Might means strength or force, as in 'with all his might', so it is a synonym for power.

clue.text: Periodical food for bird

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical
a pie is an item of food

explanation.surface: Someone puts out regular feed for the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Periodical looks like an adjective (regular), but it is a noun meaning a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white member of the crow family, common across Britain and Europe.

clue.text: Merchant promoted wine with skill

indicators.note: promoted means raised up, and in a down entry going up means reading bottom to top

parts.note: red is red wine
an art is a skill

explanation.surface: A wine dealer has been promoted for being good at the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Promoted reads as a career step for the merchant, but it is the signal to turn RED plus ART upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant buys and sells goods, which is exactly what a trader does.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic drink, abundance found in last few bars?

indicators.note: a thing found in another is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a coda is the closing passage of a piece of music
reams means a great quantity, as in reams of paper

explanation.surface: A soft drink is plentiful in the last few pubs of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Bars suggests pubs, fitting the drink; it is musical bars, and the closing ones form a coda.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet, vanilla-flavoured fizzy soft drink containing no alcohol.

clue.text: Tasteless, as is fondue?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cheap, corny and lacking refinement
second meaning: made of or tasting of melted cheese, like the Swiss dish

explanation.walkthrough: Tasteless seems to describe bland food, but means vulgar; fondue is a Swiss dish of melted cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both corny or in poor taste and literally full of cheese, which a fondue is.

clue.text: Tree that's old, as it happens

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: A remark that a tree is, as it turns out, ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: As it happens reads as 'incidentally', but means in real time, like a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean evergreen tree that bears the fruit pressed for oil.

clue.text: Pertinent European directive, ultimately

parts.note: a German is a European

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An EU directive turns out to be relevant after all.
explanation.walkthrough: European directive reads as an EU regulation, but European is a nationality and only the end of directive counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane and pertinent are synonyms meaning relevant to the matter under discussion.

clue.text: Well, face friendly

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like well!
dial is British slang for face

explanation.surface: A remark that someone has a friendly-looking face.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise, and dial is old British slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial welcome is warm and sincere, so cordial is a synonym for amicable or genial.

clue.text: Box, for example

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes for example look like an aside, but example is itself the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a container such as a suitcase and an instance or occurrence of something.

clue.text: Held by FBI, names somewhat disorganised

indicators.note: something held by another is kept within it, so the letters sit inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words, ignoring spaces and punctuation

explanation.surface: Someone detained by the FBI gives names in a somewhat muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the last letter of FBI, all of names, and the first letter of somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a mess means being untidy or chaotic, which is what disorganised describes.

clue.text: Doctor in rush, running

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A doctor dashing about in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Running suggests the doctor's haste, but it means switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical doctor who specialises in operations.
